SKAVA Discovery tab¶

The SKAVA tab in the Data Hub queries a data discovery service of the SKA Regional Centre network, SKAVA (VisIVOLab/SKAVA) or any service that speaks the IVOA standards, and opens the datasets it finds where they are: on the VisIVO backend of the node that holds the copy, when SKAVA advertises one, so that nothing is transferred. The same tab runs cutouts, moment maps, PV diagrams and source finders on that node, and shows the result in VisIVO.

How the flow works¶

[SKAVA tab]  →  GET /discovery/search  (or TAP on ivoa.obscore)
                 → matching datasets, each with the replicas ranked by SKAVA
                   and the reason for the ranking
[user picks one]
[Open]       →  GET /datalink/{obs_id}  (or the row's DataLink document)
                 → the replicas, the VisIVO backend on each node, the node's
                   SODA and product services
             →  routing: the first registered backend in SKAVA's order
             →  POST /v1/datasets/open_skava on that backend: opened in place
                 (a refusal moves on to the next node; a download through the
                 local backend is the last resort)

Discovery is metadata only: the service holds an ObsCore catalogue plus the replicas and their routing. The files stay on the nodes. The desktop talks to a node only through the VisIVO backend registered for it (Settings ▸ Backends), with that backend’s token.

Discovery service¶

The box at the top of the tab (saved in the settings, shared with the Settings dialog) has two rows, the service and the token; the endpoints a default deployment never sets are folded under Advanced:

Field

Meaning

Service (protocol)

SKAVA JSON API (SKAVA’s own endpoints) or IVOA TAP + DataLink (ADQL on ivoa.obscore and DataLink VOTables, what the SRCNet global services speak).

Service (URL)

The service’s base URL.

Token

A bearer token pasted by hand, or the one obtained with Sign in….

Sign in… / IAM…

OpenID Connect sign-in to the IAM the service trusts (the SRCNet IAM, or Keycloak on a testbed), as a public client with vlva://callback as redirect URI. IAM… sets the endpoints, the client id and the scope. A service that answers 401 with an ivoa_bearer challenge names its IAM’s discovery document, and the tab configures the endpoints from it on its own. The sign-in is kept in the system’s secure store, so the next start signs in silently.

Advanced: TAP URL, DataLink URL

For the IVOA protocol: the TAP service (/sync is appended) and the DataLink service used when a TAP row carries no DataLink access_url of its own. Empty: SKAVA’s own /tap and /datalink/<id>.

Advanced: Broker URL

A Computing Broker (the SRCNet job API) that places and runs the source finder next to the data. Empty: the finder runs as a task on the dataset’s node, started by the desktop.

When a request comes back 401, the tab offers to sign in and repeats the request afterwards.

Filters¶

The Filters section (fold it away with its arrow to give the results more room) mirrors the ObsCore parameters of GET /discovery/search and of the ADQL query built for TAP. All filters combine with AND; leave a field blank to skip it.

Field

What it sends

Notes

Position: RA / Dec / radius (deg)

POS=CIRCLE <ra> <dec> <radius>

RA in [0, 360], Dec in [-90, 90].

Band: min / max + unit

BAND=<λ_min> <λ_max> (metres)

The unit selector (MHz / GHz / Hz / m) converts your input to metres, the unit the services expect.

Time: MJD min / max

TIME=<mjd_min> <mjd_max>

Modified Julian Date.

Dataset: collection

COLLECTION=<value>

ObsCore obs_collection.

type

DPTYPE=<value>

image, cube, timeseries, spectrum.

obs_id

obs_id=<value>

Exact match.

limit / offset

pagination

limit ≤ 1000.

Results table¶

The table and the provenance of the selected row share the rest of the tab; drag the divider between them. Short columns fit their content, the Why column takes the remaining width, and a cell cut short shows its whole text on hover.

Column

Source

obs_id

metadata.obs_id (hover for the title)

Target

metadata.target_name

Type

metadata.dataproduct_type

Sky position

s_ra / s_dec

Band

em_min / em_max, shown in MHz / GHz / μm

Time

t_min / t_max (MJD)

Served by

the node SKAVA ranked first, and how many other replicas there are

Why

SKAVA’s reason for that ranking: with the resource-aware policy the measured round trip, CPU pressure, queue and memory margin of the node; with the static policy the declared scores

Hover Served by or Why for the whole decision: every replica in ranking order with its cost, reason and the age of the telemetry it was judged on.

Opening a dataset¶

Open (or a double-click on the row) resolves the dataset’s DataLink and opens it:

  1. The DataLink lists the replicas in SKAVA’s order and, for each node, the VisIVO backend co-located with it (visivo-backend service descriptor, or the #auxiliary row pointing at the backend’s /v1/node/status in the VOTable).

  2. The desktop takes the first node whose backend is registered in Settings ▸ Backends, opens the dataset in place there (POST /v1/datasets/open_skava with the replica’s file:// URL), and shows the viewer. The backend badge in the status bar names the node; its tooltip gives SKAVA’s reason.

  3. If that backend refuses, the next node in the ranking is tried, and the status bar says so. When no node can serve it, the tab explains why for each descriptor and, when SKAVA advertises a backend that is not registered, offers to register it (or to enter its token).

  4. An http(s) replica with no co-located backend is downloaded through the local backend (POST /v1/datasets/open_url).

Open via… lists the replicas with SKAVA’s reasons: pick one to open on that node instead of the first-ranked one.

The dataset is added to the Recent Datasets panel with the catalogue it came from, the protocol, the replica and the node that served it, so a reopen asks the same service again (and routes afresh) rather than reusing a path that may have moved.

How the desktop picks a node¶

The DataLink answer lists, in SKAVA’s ranking order, the VisIVO backend of each node that holds a replica (a visivo-backend service descriptor in the JSON API, one marked enabled: false being ignored; the #auxiliary row pointing at the backend’s /v1/node/status in the VOTable). The desktop goes through them in that order and keeps, as candidates, those it can use:

  1. A registered backend matches the descriptor. First by URL, against every entry of Settings ▸ Backends (the local backend included), then by the entry’s SRC code against the descriptor’s node code (exact and case-sensitive). The URL comparison ignores a trailing / and treats localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and host.docker.internal as the same host; the port and the path must match. The SRC code is for a backend the desktop reaches at another address than the catalogue advertises (a tunnel, a VPN).

  2. The backend opens this kind of dataset: the descriptor’s supports_kinds includes the dataset’s type (a timeseries or dynamic spectrum counts as dynspec).

  3. There is a token for it when the descriptor says the backend requires authentication: the one stored with the registered entry or, for the local backend registered without one, the automatic token described below.

  4. SKAVA lists a replica on that node. The desktop opens that node’s own copy: it never hands one node’s path to another node’s backend.

The candidates are tried in order (Open via… puts the chosen node first, the others keep SKAVA’s order). A file:// replica is opened in place (POST /v1/datasets/open_skava); an http(s) replica is fetched by that node’s backend (POST /v1/datasets/open_url there), still next to the data. When a backend refuses (offline, wrong token, file missing, outside its data roots), the next candidate is tried, the status bar says so, and the desktop logs [skava] backend <id> refused open: <reason>. With no candidate left, an http(s) copy is downloaded through the local backend, which forwards the SKAVA token to the storage; a file:// copy cannot be, and the dialog lists why each descriptor was passed over and offers Register backend… or Enter backend token….

Each registered backend is sent its own token and no other. The automatic token, VISIVO_TOKEN or ~/.visivo_token, belongs to the desktop’s local backend and is sent only to the configured local backend’s address (a loopback host on the local backend’s port, http://127.0.0.1:8000 by default), never to another backend, even one on the same machine at another port. A tunnel to a cluster backend therefore uses another local port: the cluster helper’s default, 18900, already does (see Running the backend on a cluster).

On the node, open_skava accepts only a file:// URL on the local host and refuses a path outside the backend’s data roots (VISIVO_DATA_ROOT or VISIVO_DATA_ROOTS, when set); the refusal comes back as valid: false with the reason, which moves the desktop to the next candidate.

Compute next to data¶

The Compute next to data… menu runs on the node, through the services SKAVA’s DataLink advertises for the dataset (node-soda-sync, node-soda-async, visivo-moment, visivo-pv as JSON descriptors; the #cutout and #proc rows with their adhoc:service descriptors in the VOTable). The product stays in the node’s workspace and is opened from there.

  • SODA cutout…: a POS (CIRCLE or POLYGON), BAND and/or TIME subset, submitted to the node’s /soda/async as a UWS job (PHASE=RUN), polled until it ends, then opened in place. Without an advertised SODA job service, the backend’s own /v1/datasets/cutout route is used.

  • Moment map…: OPERATION=MOMENT with the order (0, 1, 2), an optional channel range and threshold.

  • PV diagram…: OPERATION=PV with the path’s vertices (degrees) and the slice width in pixels.

  • Source finder…: the finders the node offers (GET /v1/finders: SoFiA-2 for cubes, photutils for images) with their parameters. With a Broker URL set, the job goes to the Computing Broker (POST /v1/jobs), which asks SKAVA where to run it, keeps to the nodes that have the finder and the memory it needs (each node states how much its finders need per byte of dataset in GET /v1/node/status; the desktop sends no memory figure of its own) and starts the finder on that node’s backend; otherwise the desktop opens the dataset on the first-ranked node and starts the finder there as a task (POST /v1/tasks/sourcefind). The dialog follows the run’s log, can cancel it, and opens the mask (as a cube) and the catalogue (VOTable) from the node.

The desktop calls a node’s service at the address of the backend registered for that node (the DataLink names the node as the catalogue sees it, which need not be reachable from the desktop), with that backend’s token.

Running a backend as an SRC node¶

The node side, what a backend next to the data serves to the desktop and to a catalogue (node status and metrics, status reports to the catalogue, SODA, source finders) and the settings it needs, is described in The backend as an SRC node. Starting a backend on a SLURM compute node, with the SSH tunnel from the laptop, the Apptainer images and server-side rendering on the node’s GPUs, is described in Running the backend on a cluster.

Common failure modes¶

  • SKAVA base URL is not configured: fill the URL before searching.

  • … requires a sign-in: the service answered 401. Sign in, or paste a token.

  • no_available_nodes - No available nodes for dataset …: the catalogue knows the dataset but cannot reach any node that holds it: the node’s backend is stopped, or the tunnel to it is closed. It probes its nodes every few seconds, so a node that comes back is used again by itself.

  • Search failed: invalid_query - POS must be ...: the spatial filter was rejected; set RA, Dec and radius together, or none.

  • “… is stored on an SRC node and can only be opened by the VisIVO backend running there”: no registered backend matches the nodes holding the dataset. Register the node’s backend (the dialog offers to), or check its token.

  • “SKAVA advertises no moment service”: the dataset is not a cube, or the node’s backend predates the operation; open the dataset and compute in the viewer instead.
